nodes.summary: A partition of actions into input, output and internal actions (Lynch and Tuttle, 1989, §3.1).
nodes.title: Action signature

nodes.summary: They are the actions of either component.
nodes.title: Actions of a composed signature

nodes.summary: All its input, output and internal actions.
nodes.title: Actions of a signature

nodes.summary: A finite sequence $\beta$ of external actions of a composition whose projections onto the two components are behaviours of the components is a behaviour of the composition (Lynch and Tuttle, 1989, Proposition 3, which they state for schedules and then "when acts() and scheds() are replaced by ext() and behs()"; here for two automata and finite behaviours). With the projection of behaviours, the finite behaviours of…
nodes.title: Pasting behaviours of the components of a composition

nodes.summary: Projection of a behaviour of a composition onto its first component (Lynch and Tuttle, 1989, Proposition 1, for finite behaviours).
nodes.title: Projection of a behaviour of a composition onto its first component

nodes.summary: Projection of a behaviour of a composition onto its second component (Lynch and Tuttle, 1989, Proposition 1, for finite behaviours).
nodes.title: Projection of a behaviour of a composition onto its second component

nodes.summary: The external actions of a finite schedule, in order (Lynch and Tuttle, 1989, §3.1).
nodes.title: Finite behaviour of an I/O automaton

nodes.summary: The composition of two strongly compatible automata (Lynch and Tuttle, 1989, §3.2, for two automata). Its states are pairs of states. An action of the composition moves each component that has it in its signature by one of its transitions, and leaves the other component unchanged; a shared action is therefore taken simultaneously by both components, which is how an output of one is received as an input by the…
nodes.title: Composition of I/O automata

nodes.summary: Composition of action signatures (Lynch and Tuttle, 1989, §3.2). Outputs are the outputs of either component, internal actions the internal actions of either, and inputs the inputs of either that are output by neither.
nodes.title: Composition of action signatures

nodes.summary: The subsequence of the actions of `β` that are external actions of `S`.
nodes.title: External projection

nodes.summary: Its input and output actions.
nodes.title: External actions of a signature

nodes.summary: An action signature, a nonempty set of start states and a labelled transition system whose transitions are labelled by actions of the signature and which is input-enabled: every input action is enabled in every state (Lynch and Tuttle, 1989, §3.1). Input-enabledness expresses that an automaton cannot block its environment: it controls only its outputs and internal actions.
nodes.title: Input/output automaton

nodes.summary: If every action of `β` is an action of a component and the projections of `β` label finite executions of the components from `s.1` to `t₁` and from `s.2` to `t₂`, then `β` labels a finite execution of the composition from `s` to `(t₁, t₂)`.
nodes.title: Pasting executions of the components of a composition

nodes.summary: A finite execution of the composition projects to a finite execution of the first component, along the actions of that component.
nodes.title: Projection of an execution of a composition onto its first component

nodes.summary: A finite execution of the composition projects to a finite execution of the second component, along the actions of that component.
nodes.title: Projection of an execution of a composition onto its second component

nodes.summary: Each is an action of one of the components.
nodes.title: External actions of a composition

nodes.summary: An external action of a composition that is an action of the first component is an external action of it, and conversely.
nodes.title: External actions of a composition in its first component

nodes.summary: An external action of a composition that is an action of the second component is an external action of it, and conversely.
nodes.title: External actions of a composition in its second component

nodes.summary: An action of a signature that is not internal is external.
nodes.title: Non-internal actions are external

nodes.summary: For an action `a`, the component `A` moves from `s` to `t` by a transition labelled `a` if `a` is one of its actions, and stays put otherwise.
nodes.title: Component move in a composition

nodes.summary: Internal actions are not external.
nodes.title: Internal actions are not external

nodes.summary: Keeping the external actions of the composition and then the actions of the first component gives the external actions of the first component among its actions.
nodes.title: Projection onto the first component and external projection commute

nodes.summary: Keeping the external actions of the composition and then the actions of the second component gives the external actions of the second component among its actions.
nodes.title: Projection onto the second component and external projection commute

nodes.summary: The subsequence of the actions of `β` that are actions of `S` (written `β|A` by Lynch and Tuttle).
nodes.title: Projection onto a signature

nodes.summary: A finite sequence $\beta$ of actions of a composition whose projections onto the two components are schedules of the components is a schedule of the composition (Lynch and Tuttle, 1989, Proposition 3, for two automata and finite schedules). With the projection of schedules this characterizes the finite schedules of a composition by those of its components.
nodes.title: Pasting schedules of the components of a composition

nodes.summary: Projection of a schedule of a composition onto its first component (Lynch and Tuttle, 1989, Proposition 1, for finite schedules).
nodes.title: Projection of a schedule of a composition onto its first component

nodes.summary: Projection of a schedule of a composition onto its second component (Lynch and Tuttle, 1989, Proposition 1, for finite schedules).
nodes.title: Projection of a schedule of a composition onto its second component

nodes.summary: The sequence of actions of a finite execution from a start state (Lynch and Tuttle, 1989, §3.1).
nodes.title: Finite schedule of an I/O automaton

nodes.summary: Strongly compatible signatures (Lynch and Tuttle, 1989, §3.2, for two signatures): their output actions are disjoint, and the internal actions of each are not actions of the other.
nodes.title: Strongly compatible signatures

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
